newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks take heavy hit at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks take heavy hit at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks pulled sharply back Wednesday to close at session lows, dogged by a political slanging-match over corruption cover-up charges and by currency jitters in Mexico, dealers said.
"The political issue is serious, because every day we hear new comments about government officials, which is bad news," said analyst Cristina Hintz at brokers Provincia Bursatil.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index tumbled 3.2 percent to 560.55, erasing a partial recovery it showed at midsession.

"The selling wave was worsened by Mexico's currency woes, but I'd say the main factor in the markets in the past 48 hours has been (former Economy Minister Domingo) Cavallo's 'mafia' charges," said Jose Napoli of traders Ignoto y Napoli.

Cavallo, sacked less than three months ago by President Carlos Menem, unleashed a political storm Tuesday when he accused two cabinet ministers of hampering court investigations by manipulating judges and prosecutors.
Menem dismissed the charges, even though he himself last week launched a probe into a $3.0 billion customs smuggling ring and vowed to wage war on corruption.
Analysts said the graft debate caused the bolsa to speed up normal profit-taking after seven straight weeks of gains.

"All Brady bonds are pulling back in Latin America, and Mexico is feeling the impact of the devaluation of the peso against the dollar," said Hintz. "The combination of weak Latin American markets and the correction we all expected here was compounded by the political issue."

Napoli said while the bolsa could slip lower Thursday, the medium-term outlook remained good. "Some stocks are still hard to get because nobody wants to sell, and also (Friday's) options expirations are keeping prices in check," he said.
The all-share index fell 3.1 percent in the session, with losers smashing winners 45 to four and 12 issues closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 19 millon pesos from 15.6 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover rose to 125.7 million pesos from 114.5 million the previous session.

The day's worst main-tier losers were agricultural holding company Cresud, steelmaker Acindar and Telefonica, which all reeled 5.7 percent. Telefonica and Telecom, off 5.3 percent, were also hurt by an earnings estimate downgrade by UBS. The only MerVal riser was steelmaker Siderar, up 0.7 percent.
